To distinguish between natural photographic blur/murkiness and AI-generated smoothing or noise artifacts.
To verify that the fins are distinct entities connected correctly to the body and not fused or floating, especially given the blur.

focus_areas: Integrity of the cephalofoil (hammer head) shape and symmetry.
Connection points of all fins (dorsal, pectoral, caudal) to the main body.
Differentiation between photographic motion blur and AI generation smearing.
Consistency of lighting and shadows on the ventral vs dorsal surfaces.
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'blur' artifact. In real underwater photography, motion blur is common. However, AI often uses blur to hide malformed anatomy. Check if the blur is directional (consistent with movement) or isotropic (smearing in all directions, suggesting generation error). Verify if the cephalofoil maintains structural rigidity or if it appears to warp into the water.
